title: One Ringgit for an Airline That Was 'About Dead'
conflicts: Debt: RM40 million (Key.Aero, AFP/Daily Star, Wikipedia) = about US$11 million (Bloomberg 2004, Sunday Times 2014) at the 2001 peg; MoneyWeek says 5 million pounds; Forbes Asia 2010 says '$40 million' (apparently ringgit/dollar confusion); a 2018 Star piece mentions RM190 million in liabilities. Story uses 'some RM40 million'. Deal date: 5 or 8 September 2001 (days before 9/11) vs a Mahathir meeting in October 2001 (Bloomberg) and 'shortly after' 9/11 (AFP), completion 2 December 2001 (Tune Group page); story says accounts differ. First flight 8 January vs relaunch 15 January 2002; story says January 2002.
notes: This is my one edition that mentions talQen (in the reflection, on weighing a larger step). The 'about dead' quotation, the six-per-cent statistic and the Mahathir meeting come from Fernandes's keynote as retold in a Sunday Times (Singapore) column, so they are attributed to his later account and Mahathir is paraphrased, not quoted; that PDF loads but the checker cannot read its text. Quote stance is challenges.
